title: Viper Image That Caused Alarm in California Was A.I.-Generated

reading.body:
This is a fabricated-evidence failure. An AI-generated image was presented as a photograph of a specific animal at a specific place, and it was convincing enough that a police department treated it as a real sighting and issued a public safety warning. The failure did not occur inside a model's training or deployment in any ordinary sense. It occurred at the point where a synthetic image entered a human process, the police alert, that had no step for verifying whether the image was real.

The cost fell on the responders rather than on anyone who saw the image. Herpetologists were brought in and an area was searched for a snake that was never there. Catching this would have required someone in the chain, before the warning went out, to ask where the image came from and to check it against the physical facts. A four to five foot Gaboon viper in a residential tree in California is already an unlikely claim, and the image was the only thing supporting it.

What is not established is who generated the image, why, or whether anyone intended the police to act on it. The reporting does not say what happens next, so no consequence for the person or persons responsible is known.

reports.title: Viper Image That Caused Alarm in California Was A.I.-Generated

summary:
Police in Santa Ana, California, warned residents about a highly venomous Gaboon viper said to have been spotted in a tree in a residential neighborhood. The snake was estimated at four to five feet long, far from its native rainforests in equatorial Africa. The alert told people not to approach or handle it. Herpetologists were called in and the area was searched, but no snake or evidence of one was found.

The image presented as proof of the sighting turned out to be fake, generated by artificial intelligence. The article does not say what happens next.
